label: Born in Philadelphia
description: Vera Rubin was born in 1928, just shy of her fifth birthday in 1933.

sources.quote: Just shy of Rubin's fifth birthday, in 1933

label: Moved to Washington D.C.
description: Rubin's family moved south to Washington D.C. around 1933.

sources.quote: Around this time, Rubin, her parents, and her older sister moved south to Washington D.C.

label: Enrolled at Vassar College
description: Rubin packed her bags and headed for New York's Hudson Valley in the fall of 1945.

sources.quote: in the fall of 1945, she packed her bags and headed for New York's Hudson Valley.

label: Married Robert Rubin
description: Rubin fell in love with Robert Rubin prior to her final year at Vassar and had a summer wedding in 1948.

sources.quote: Prior to her final year, she fell in love with Robert Rubin, and by the fall of 1947 was engaged. Not yet twenty, she was looking forward to a summer wedding

label: Started Master's at Cornell
description: Rubin joined her husband at Cornell University to earn a master's degree in astronomy.

sources.quote: Rubin joined her husband at Cornell University, where he was working on his doctoral degree in physics.

label: Presented at AAS Meeting
description: Rubin presented her research at the 1950 winter meeting of the American Astronomical Society.

sources.quote: her thesis advisor, William Shaw, thought the results should be discussed at the 1950 winter meeting of the American Astronomical Society

label: Awarded Ph.D.
description: Rubin received her Ph.D. from Georgetown University in 1954.

sources.quote: The avant-garde conclusion earned Rubin her Ph.D. in 1954

label: Moved back to Washington D.C.
description: The Rubins moved back to D.C. during the summer of 1960.

sources.quote: During the summer of 1960, the Rubins, now with four children, moved back to D.C.

label: Published Milky Way Rotation Curve
description: Rubin and her students published findings on the Milky Way's rotation curve in 1962.

sources.quote: The rotation curve she and her students drew for the Milky Way was unexpectedly, well, flat. ... This was 1962.

label: Moved to San Diego
description: In 1963, Rubin's husband received a fellowship that took the family to UC San Diego.

sources.quote: In 1963, her husband received a fellowship that took the family to the University of California in San Diego

label: Started at DTM
description: Rubin first showed up for work at the Department of Terrestrial Magnetism on April Fools day 1965.

sources.quote: Rubin first showed up for work on April Fools day.

label: Started Andromeda Observations
description: Rubin and Ford set out to Kitt Peak to study Andromeda in 1967.

sources.quote: It was 1967. The observatory had a fairly new 84-inch telescope and the two decided to use it.

label: Published Andromeda Paper
description: Results were published in the Astrophysical Journal in February 1970.

sources.quote: the results were published in the Astrophysical Journal in February 1970.

label: Dark Matter Halo Proposed
description: Princeton theorists proposed the dark matter halo hypothesis in 1973.

sources.quote: in 1973 the theorists officially proposed their striking hypothesis

label: 4-Meter Telescope Opened
description: A larger telescope opened at Kitt Peak in 1974.

sources.quote: In 1974, an even larger telescope, one with a mirror four meters or 158 inches wide, opened at Kitt Peak.

label: Kitt Peak Observing Run
description: Rubin conducted an observing run at Kitt Peak in November 2007.

sources.quote: Tonight and tomorrow are her last two in the fourteen-night observing run she is doing with Hunter.
